results.notes: What was built. Migration 0058 adds review_state, source_run_id, source_thread_id and proposal_reason to agent_skills (existing rows read accepted), replaces the unique key (org_id, name) with (org_id, scope, owner_user_id, name), and adds a partial index on proposed rows. Proto is additive at the reserved tags: UpsertAgentSkillRequest 10-15, UpsertAgentSkillResponse 4-5, ListAgentSkillsRequest 3, AgentSkill 13-18. session-core: a background_review upsert is forced to a disabled, user-scoped, proposed row owned by owner_user_id. It checks the memory and org-policy gate under the owner's row lock and returns a closed skip_reason (memory_state, org_policy, zdr, owner_required, protected, accepted_exists, rejected_exists). The conflict arm refreshes content and provenance on proposed learned rows only, never enabled/scope/owner/review_state. A human upsert cannot switch on a proposal. set_agent_skill_enabled refuses to enable a non-accepted row (failed_precondition proposal_requires_decision). list_agent_skills honours for_user_id for service callers only, hides proposals from share grantees, orders by name then scope DESC, and returns the new fields. capability-core: SessionRef.UserID; the review asks GetMemoryControls before any transcript read when the WithMemoryControls option is given (fail closed, retried on error; skips memory_state, org_policy, owner_unknown); the transcript source lists skills as the run owner; the sink writes a disabled user-scoped proposal with run, thread and reason and stops the batch on a policy refusal; learning gained Reason (cut to 300), the Screen hook (no-op), and a prompt asking for a reason; the registry returns origin, review_state, source_run_id, proposal_reason, hides proposals from grantees and admins, and refuses enabling a non-accepted skill with 409 proposal_requires_decision inside the UPDATE. model-gateway: skills.rs got per-pull Org and User(caller) buckets with a ref-counted holder book (refresh_learned replaces is_org_loaded/replace_learned/skill_ownership_entries), source_path prefixes session-core:org: and session-core:user:<owner>:, learned entries matched with usable (fail closed) while disk skills keep usable_or_untracked, the caller's own skill wins a name tie, and only owner-accepted rows are cached; grpc.rs, sse.rs and tool_loop.rs use it (reattach_skill drops non-accepted rows). verify-durable-layer.sh G7 was rewritten for the new conflict key (needs the lead's docker run).

results.notes:
Built with every switch untouched (the slice adds none). model-gateway: GET/PUT /v1/memories/controls and POST /v1/memories/reset, user bearer only, with org and user taken from the claims. PUT accepts only the literal words on, paused, off. Reset needs confirm:true at the gateway as well as in session-core, and is not ZDR-blocked because it only erases. session_memory_error now maps FailedPrecondition to a typed 409 {error:{code,details.reason}}. This covers memory_not_enabled:<reason> from IndexMemory and the ZDR refusal of SetMemoryControls; both were a 502 before, and no other branch changed. The plan's route list does not name this mapping, but 'remember' needs it to report a paused refusal honestly.

BFF (domains/memory.rs): GET/PUT /api/v1/memory/controls, POST /api/v1/memory/reset, POST /api/v1/memory (remember), all behind the existing require_session and rate-limit layers. Only state, confirm, threadId and content are forwarded, so a client cannot name another user. Five wiremock tests were added: only state is forwarded, confirm is forwarded as false rather than defaulted, a paused refusal comes back as 409, empty content makes no upstream hop, and the controls read goes upstream as a GET.

Actions: memory.set_state (low, reversible), memory.reset (high, requiresApproval, not reversible, input confirm: z.literal(true)) and memory.remember (low). Dispatchers and handler arms were added. All three are human-only.

SPA: memory-client gained getMemoryControls, setMemoryState, resetMemory and rememberMemory. An unknown state becomes null and a missing flag becomes 'not allowed', never 'on'. MemorySection has an On/Pause/Off radiogroup, override banners for org_disabled, zdr and policy_unavailable, a hidden-rows note, and a two-step Reset with cancel. Under ZDR the selector is locked but Reset stays available. ChatMessages: one 'Husk dette' button and one handler on the assistant message, hidden in temporary chat or without a thread. A paused refusal shows its own note and never 'Husket'. i18n nb/en is inline through i18n.tr, like the rest of the file.
